title: Finite biproduct equivalence for invertible curve assertions
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $k$ a field, $X$ a scheme and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.
Let $I$ be a finite index type and $G_a$ module sheaves on the small etale site of $X$.
Let $H$ be a module sheaf equipped with an isomorphism $e:H\simeq\bigoplus_a G_a$,
using finite biproducts [def-weil-additive-category]. The predicates $C_1,\ldots,C_8$
are those of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], with their stated conditional hypotheses.
Let $r$ be prime and suppose $r\operatorname{id}_{G_a}=0$ for every $a$ and
$r\operatorname{id}_H=0$. Assume $G_a$ and $H$ constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf].
Then $C_4(H)\land C_6(H)$ holds if and only if $C_4(G_a)\land C_6(G_a)$ holds for every $a$.
Invertible-order torsion has the stalk meaning of [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion].

source.place: Theorem 03SC, proof, fourth paragraph; Lemma 0A5C. Primary text checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SC and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A5C.

proof.text: If r is invertible in k, every stalk of each G a and H has invertible-order torsion, since r kills it. Constructibility of the finite sum and transport along e supply the C4 hypothesis for H. Cohomology and inverse image are additive and comparison maps natural, so finiteness and bijectivity are equivalent to the same properties for all components. This proves both C4 and C6 in this case. If r is not invertible in the field k, the characteristic is r. Any r-killed sheaf with invertible-order torsion has zero stalks: each stalk element is killed by r and by an integer invertible in k, hence coprime to r; Bezout then kills it by 1. Stalk conservativity makes it the zero sheaf. Its cohomology is zero, finite, and all comparison maps bijective. This proves all exceptional conditional assertions for H and for any individual component. Empty sums are zero. Here cohomology means the Ext-based Sheaf.H occurring in the eight predicates: Sheaf.functorH is additive, and Ext.addEquivBiproduct gives the finite product of component groups. No identification with derived global sections is used.

lean.statement:
theorem prime_biproduct_invertible_iff (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (r : ℕ) [Fact r.Prime] {ι : Type} [Finite ι]
    (G : ι → Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (hGc : ∀ a, Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf (G a)) (hGr : ∀ a, r • 𝟙 (G a) = 0)
    {H : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)} (e : H ≅ ⨁ G)
    (hHr : r • 𝟙 H = 0)
    (hHc : Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf H) :
    (FiniteOfInvertibleOrder Λ H k ∧ BaseChangeOfInvertibleOrder Λ f H) ↔
      ∀ a, FiniteOfInvertibleOrder Λ (G a) k ∧
        BaseChangeOfInvertibleOrder Λ f (G a)
